name: substrate-card the semantic ladder and its generators -- qualify, do not fix
description: MINTED 2026-08-26 by 1.0.0_SA_CTO~X on Andrew-direct at the CTO~X terminal. VERBATIM: 'I would put this as Directive 11, Substrate Analysis, and register a project beneath it called NFRA_SUBSTRATECARDING.' Runs CLAUDE.md Rule 28 (THE SUBSTRATE TEST, @ec35b78c1c) across every rung, rail and generator the C3.i identity work will stand on, producing one machine-checkable SUBSTRATE CARD per subject against org/standards/SUBSTRATE_CARD.schema.json. QUALIFY-ONLY, ZERO FIXES -- the same posture as NFRA_DEPLOYCENSUS: a card names a defect and its OWNER, it does not remediate, and a finding is never a dispatch. THE END GOAL IS NOT THE CARDS: Andrew, verbatim -- 'the end goal is to basically develop a mechanical process around the materialization and tracking of c3.i'. The four-stage identity pipeline (affinity compilation -> similarity network fusion -> identity -> succession) cannot be built on substrate whose grain, state, coverage, key space and failure modes are unknown, and six separate id-space defects were measured in one day while trying. WAVE 1 SUBJECTS (bounded, known): C0, C1, C2, C3.i-as-built, D1, D2, D3, and whatever underlies comp-similar. WAVE 2 IS DERIVED, NOT GUESSED: questions 1 and 4 of every wave-1 card NAME the generators and storage locations, so the wave-2 subject list falls out of wave-1 output rather than being enumerated up front. SEPARATE STANDING DELIVERABLE: a graph-object manifest -- what graph stores exist, which are heavy/authoritative vs light/traversable projections, and each tagged to its generator -- assembled from the projection_of lineage the cards carry. Andrew's concern, verbatim: 'something that is very concerning to me is not having a clear manifest of what graph objects exist and where involved in this process'.
phase: REGISTERED 2026-08-26. Rule 28 landed @ec35b78c1c; card contract landed at org/standards/SUBSTRATE_CARD.schema.json (Draft 2020-12 valid, negative control rejects an empty card). Awaiting purpose-level PRD ratification then COO atom-decomp per Rule 27 -- no TO cut, no lane seated. One card already exercised ahead of the project as the reference example: nerves_resolve (design SOUND; cadence NONE, persistence NONE, substrate 19.7d stale, coverage 2,249 of ~27,000 nodes, failure mode SILENT, self-test RED). || 2026-08-26 WAVE 1 DISPATCHED by 2.0.0_SA_COO~X: decomp nfra-substratecarding/20260826T172918Z @aae317509b, 61 cells over two declared planes, 4 TOs (CCX C0/C1/C2 | CCY D1/D2/D3 | COX C3.i+comp-similar | DTX graph-object manifest). 3.0.0_SA_CVO~X seated as proof-of-spec verifier. || SCHEMA v2 AUTHORED, EFFECTIVE AT THE WAVE BOUNDARY -- NOT MID-WAVE. COO~X exercised v1 during the decomp (finding 72935) and found THREE requirements living in prose a validator cannot branch on: F-1 a null coverage denominator validates; F-2 determinism=inferential validates with NO inference_detail because 'REQUIRED when...' sat in a description string; F-3 verdict SOUND validates while a row carries basis=absent. All three are the CLAUDE.md section-4 defect this project exists to measure, committed inside the project's own contract. v1 REMAINS THE FREEZE FOR WAVE 1 (Rule 27: mid-round the spec is frozen; 4 TOs and a staged verifier harness reference it, and COO~X already carries all three as TO acceptance criteria AC3/AC4/AC5). org/standards/SUBSTRATE_CARD.v2.schema.json makes them MECHANICAL for wave 2 so nothing depends on anyone remembering. Exercised: all 3 ACCEPT on v1 and REJECT on v2, with two positive controls (a fully-measured SOUND card passes; a null denominator WITH a stated reason passes). || OWED AT THE WAVE BOUNDARY, recorded so it does not decay: the L0 manifest's lineage.projection_of and co_resident_stores are STILL array-of-string and carry the same identity-jammed-into-description defect that SUBSTRATE_CARD v2 just fixed with $defs/joinable_ref (id + note, id REJECTING ' -- ' and ' ('). NOT APPLIED MID-WAVE -- 0.4.0_DT_ClientPlatform~X is writing SC-m-3 against the L0 schema right now and 2.0.0_SA_COO~X ruled this explicitly not a mid-wave act. Source finding: COO~X 73294 @d94e825bf2 -- 51 raw entries across 8 cards resolving to 43 distinct subjects, 6 with multiple spellings; a consumer at face value enumerates 51 parts where 43 exist, and THE OVER-COUNT LOOKS LIKE THOROUGHNESS. No lane could have avoided it while following the schema; the defect was the field type. || ⛔ ARCHITECTURAL CONSEQUENCE, owed at the wave boundary and STRONGER than the joinable_ref fix it supersedes in scope: 2.0.0_SA_COO~X's tension proof (73329) shows NO DEDUP HEURISTIC ON THESE FIELDS CAN BE CORRECT -- a key strict enough to catch false splits MERGES kuzu_nessie_db with s3://opal-estate-report/kuzu_nessie_db (two distinct objects, 82.5MB local vs 51.0MB in-bucket, corroborated independently at the CTO~X seat), and a key loose enough to keep them apart leaves the splits. THE IDENTITY IS NOT IN THE STRING. Therefore joinable_ref {id,note} is NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT: it separates identity from description but a clean id 'kuzu_nessie_db' still names two objects. THE L0 MANIFEST MUST BECOME THE REGISTRY -- minting part_id per part, with cards REFERENCING a registered part_id rather than a free-text name. Same L1-entity-spine problem one layer down, which is why it recurs: free-text names have been asked to do an identity registry's job. NOT BUILT, NOT AMENDED MID-WAVE.
blocking: Not blocked. Sequencing only: Rule 27 runs register -> purpose-level PRD -> COO atom-decomp -> TO -> execute. Lanes must NOT start before the decomp exists or five seats freelance and produce five overlapping reads. A FROZEN card template plus one worked example must precede dispatch, or N lanes mint N card dialects -- which would be this project self-inflicting the exact defect it exists to measure.
